candidates.summary: Google's Bring Your Own Agent feature lets Claude Agent, Codex, Antigravity, and custom enterprise harnesses use Android Studio's optimized tools and context.
candidates.what_changed: Android Studio's Bring Your Own Agent feature allows external coding agents—including Claude Agent, Codex, and Antigravity—to operate through Android Studio's optimized infrastructure and tools.
candidates.why_it_matters: IDE vendors are moving from bundling one assistant toward becoming **agent execution platforms**. That reduces lock-in and lets teams keep their preferred harness while reusing IDE-native Android context and tooling.

candidates.title: Google Cloud API Gateway can expose existing REST APIs as MCP tools
candidates.summary: Teams can annotate an OpenAPI spec and let API Gateway act as a remote MCP server without standing up a separate agent-facing service.
candidates.what_changed: Google Cloud API Gateway can now act as a remote MCP server. Existing REST operations become agent-callable tools by annotating the OpenAPI definition instead of recreating routing, authentication, and quota logic in a new MCP service.
candidates.why_it_matters: MCP adoption gets much easier when **existing API governance becomes the agent boundary**. Enterprises can expose capabilities without duplicating infrastructure and security policy.

candidates.title: A survey maps how coding agents can evolve from their own execution history
candidates.summary: The literature now spans agents that update memory, skills, tools, framework logic, models, or collaboration structures using executable feedback from prior coding work.
candidates.what_changed: A new survey organizes work on coding agents that change themselves from prior interactions: updating memory, skills, tools, framework behavior, models, or collaboration structures.
candidates.why_it_matters: Self-improvement needs the same disciplines as deployment: **reversibility, evaluation, provenance, and controlled promotion of learned behavior**.

candidates.title: GitHub Security Lab builds an autonomous fuzzing Taskflow Agent
candidates.summary: The fuzzing taskflow lets an agent inspect coverage, write harnesses, execute fuzzers, triage crashes, and iterate instead of stopping at one generated test.
candidates.what_changed: GitHub Security Lab's fuzzing Taskflow uses an agent to handle work that normally keeps continuous fuzzing human-intensive: inspect coverage gaps, build new harnesses, run fuzzers, analyze crashes, and iterate.
candidates.why_it_matters: Security automation becomes much more valuable when the agent owns a **verified loop**, not just code generation. Fuzzer coverage and crashes provide concrete external signals the agent cannot talk its way around.

sources.label: GitHub Security Lab — AI-powered fuzzing with the Taskflow Agent
